title: Redwood Security Review - SSO/SCIM/RBAC - ClarityHealth
summary: Redwood AE+SE reviewed SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning flows and proposed RBAC roles for ClarityHealth. Discussed least-privilege, SCIM group mappings, SCIM delta sync frequency, provisioning tokens, audit log retention and export, and options for CMEK and VPC private deployments. Agreed to run a test SSO/SCIM setup in a dev tenant and share security docs and SOC2/ISO artifacts.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Maya Singh, Lucas Reed, Anita Gomez, Tom Wu (ClarityHealth)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood. quick round of intros?
[00:08] Maya: Hi, Maya, head of security at ClarityHealth, Lucas is with me, Tom's on IAM and Anita is our infra lead.
[00:14] Jordan: Great, quick agenda - SAML SSO setup, SCIM provisioning and group mappings, RBAC roles for least privilege, audit logs, and encryption/KMS options.  Any additions?
[00:25] Lucas: No, sounds good. We're mainly focused on: 1) how users map to roles, 2) how SCIM handles groups, and 3) what logs we can pull for audits.
[00:35] Priya: I'll go through the SSO flow - we support SAML 2.0, metadata exchange, and attribute mappings. We typically recommend Okta as IdP but any SAML provider works.
[00:44] Tom: Cool, we use Okta. question — can you do SCIM provisioning from Okta to Redwood, and what's the auth token model?
[00:53] Priya: Yes — we support SCIM 2.0. We issue a SCIM bearer token per customer (rotatable). The token is used by the IdP to call Redwood's /scim endpoints for user and group provisioning. Token rotation is supported via the console or API.
[01:05] Maya: and delta syncs? we need near real-time group changes for access revocation.
[01:12] Priya: We recommend delta sync every 5–15 minutes for most orgs; near real-time for highly sensitive roles you can combine SCIM with JIT on SAML assertion side. Our delta includes added/removed members and group renames. Occasionally the auto-generated delta might miss a rename if the IdP normalizes attributes — we saw that with a customer using, uh, "Okter" in the logs, so test is important.
[01:35] Lucas: how do we map groups to Redwood roles?
[01:38] Priya: Mapping is via attribute mapping in SCIM or SAML group claims. Typical roles we suggest: Admin (full), Developer (deploy + read), Analyst/ML (inference access, no infra), ReadOnly, Auditor (logs-only). You can create custom roles via the Console. We usually recommend least-priv model: only Admins get user management or SCIM tokens.
[02:00] Tom: we want separation — Security team should be able to view logs but not change infra. Auditor role sounds right. Are audit logs immutable?
[02:08] Sam: Logs are append-only in our system, we keep tamper-evident metadata, and we can export to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/S3) via push or S3 export. Retention windows configurable; default 90 days, enterprise option for longer.
[02:25] Maya: retention — we need 7 years for some workflows, how do you handle that?
[02:30] Priya: For long-term retention we recommend exporting to your S3 and enabling object lock or Glacier. Redwood can keep short-term logs for quick UI access and stream exports for long-term archival. We'll include the export playbook.
[02:45] Lucas: encryption — do you support CMEK? we need customer-managed keys in GCP KMS/AWS KMS for regulatory needs.
[02:54] Priya: Yes, we support CMEK for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with managed keys by default and an option for CMEK if on Dedicated or VPC-private plan. We'll need a service account/key with limited perms and we support key rotation.
[03:10] Anita: any specific IAM perms for KMS?
[03:13] Priya: Minimal: cryptographic encrypt/decrypt and key get metadata, plus permissions to perform key rotation if you want automation. We have a doc with least-priv KMS policy for AWS/GCP.
[03:25] Tom: SCIM provisioning — does Redwood support group-to-role mapping in the Graph/SCIM payload or do we do SAML claim mapping? Which is recommended?
[03:34] Priya: Both supported. For automated provisioning we prefer SCIM group->role mapping because it handles membership changes cleanly; SAML group claims are great for session-time assertions (JIT), but they rely on the IdP sending correct group claims. Best practice: use SCIM for canonical group membership and SAML assertions for extra session attributes.
[03:55] Maya: service accounts — who can create SCIM tokens?
[03:58] Jordan: Only Admin role can create/rotate SCIM tokens by default; you can delegate via a custom role but we recommend limiting token creation to a small set.
[04:10] Lucas: what about RBAC for model endpoints? devs can call hosted APIs but shouldn't see billing or rotate keys.
[04:18] Priya: We have per-route and per-model RBAC controls; you can scope API keys and tokens to inference-only, management-only, or full. Also audit logs capture token usage and token->user mapping when tied to SSO.
[04:33] Tom: speaking of tokens — are API keys linkable to users for auditing?
[04:37] Sam: Yes, when issued via SSO or SCIM-bound accounts we surface user identities in logs. For legacy API keys we recommend rotating and tying to service accounts.
[04:45] Maya: compliance artifacts — can you provide SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001?
[04:50] Sam: yes, we'll send the most recent reports under an NDA; also provide pen test summary and our security packet.
[04:57] Lucas: VPC/private deployment — for data residency we may need a dedicated VPC in us-east-1 and logs stored in our S3 in our account. Is that supported?
[05:06] Priya: Yes supported for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer region pushes and can configure S3 export to your account via cross-account roles. For full isolation we'd recommend Private deployment with VPC peering and optional on-prem for air-gapped.
[05:22] Anita: can we do SCIM over a private link?
[05:25] Priya: We currently support SCIM over HTTPS; for Private deployments you can expose SCIM endpoints inside your VPC or use a reverse proxy. We'll include architecture diagrams for SCIM in VPCs.
[05:35] Maya: auditability — can we get log integrity proofs or blockchain-style hashes?
[05:40] Jordan: We include tamper-evident checksums and can provide attestations for a date range. Not blockchain by default but we can discuss higher-integrity options for enterprise contracts.
[05:52] Lucas: latency concerns — does SAML add auth latency to inference? not really but just checking.
[05:57] Priya: SAML is only at session creation; inference calls use tokens/cookies so not on the critical path. KV cache and serving runtime are separate — sometimes transcripts will show "KV cache" or mis-terms but performance isn't impacted.
[06:10] Tom: what's your SCIM delta behavior on concurrent edits?
[06:13] Priya: We process SCIM deltas idempotently, and we provide conflict logs. If two provisioning actions clash the last-write wins with an audit entry. We can configure stronger semantics for Private deployments.
[06:26] Maya: ok — for least-privilege role definitions we want a proposed mapping now.
[06:30] Priya: Sure — Proposed mapping:
- Security_Audit (Auditor): view-only access to audit logs, cannot modify users or infra.
- Org_Admin (Admin): full access, manage users, SCIM tokens, billing.
- Platform_Engineer (Developer): deploy/models, manage endpoints, not billing or user mgmt.
- Analyst (ML/Analyst): run evals, read model outputs, cannot deploy infra changes.
- Service_Account (Service): non-human token for CI; scoped to inference only.

[06:55] Lucas: can we have a staging Admin and separate prod Admin?
[06:58] Priya: Yes, we encourage separate envs and role scoping per project. You can also scope roles by team and namespace.
[07:06] Tom: any limitations around SCIM group size? we have 10k users per group in some teams.
[07:10] Priya: SCIM handles large groups; delta payloads chunk. For very large groups we recommend using SCIM for membership and SAML for claims where appropriate. There have been edge cases with huge groups causing timeouts at the IdP side — ok to do incremental syncs.
[07:23] Maya: rotation policy — how often should we rotate SCIM token and CMEK keys?
[07:28] Priya: SCIM tokens quarterly is common; keys depend on your policy — 90 days to yearly. We support automated rotation workflows for CMEK in Dedicated.
[07:38] Lucas: logging format — JSON lines? can you push to our Splunk HTTP Event Collector?
[07:42] Sam: Yes, we output structured JSON, and we have forwarders for Splunk/Datadog and direct S3 export.
[07:50] Tom: demo idea — can we run a quick handshake test in dev now?
[07:53] Priya: Happy to. Jordan, do you want to coordinate a short pilot?
[07:56] Jordan: Yes — we'll schedule a 30–45 minute pilot with Tom next week, Priya will run the SCIM sync, and Sam will drop the security docs.
[08:05] Maya: great. any blockers?
[08:07] Tom: none on our side, just need the sample metadata and a SCIM token from Redwood.
[08:12] Jordan: We'll send metadata and a temporary SCIM token scoped to the test group. Token will be rotated after the test.
[08:20] Lucas: final question — can we limit API keys to specific models? we want devs to call smaller open models but not high-cost models.
[08:28] Priya: Yes, per-model routing and per-key model allowlists are available — we can enforce quotas and route to cheaper quantized variants automatically for certain keys.
[08:38] Maya: thanks all — let's recap next steps.
[08:42] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to send SAML metadata + sample mappings; Priya to run SCIM pilot and provide logs; Sam to send SOC2/ISO docs; Tom to provision Okta test tenant. Follow-up week of 12/28.
[08:55] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("Okter" vs Okta), speaker overlaps, and some product names slightly garbled (e.g., Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated) due to auto transcription.
